tldr: An empirical security study of attack propagation and structural authorization containment in a four-agent LLM pipeline, showing that signed-token authorization can prevent unsafe execution even when an upstream LLM validator is compromised.
motivation: Multi-agent LLM systems assign agents differing privilege levels, so a compromised low-privilege agent may influence a higher-privilege agent into unauthorized actions; the authors seek to understand and contain such propagation.
method: They build a four-agent LangGraph pipeline (Supervisor, Researcher, Validator, Executor) and test shared-memory poisoning and indirect prompt injection via a forged approval in a retrieved document, comparing LLM-based validation against an independent authorization layer using task-bound signed tokens and a verified policy oracle.
result: Memory poisoning reaches execution in all undefended trials; with authorization enabled it yields 100% Judgment Bypass Rate but 0% Unsafe Action Rate, and an Observer layer cuts the agent-hijacking false-positive rate from 49% to 7%.
conclusion: Structural authorization can contain compromised agent behavior even when upstream LLM judgment fails, decoupling execution security from the reliability of the validator's judgment.

title: Evaluating The Impact Of Personalization In Conversational Cybersecurity Assistants
authors: Lea Duesterwald, Anika Jain, Shreya Kochar, Norman Sadeh
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Users increasingly turn to Large Language Models to answer a variety of questions, including cybersecurity questions. We study how personalization strategies can help improve the effectiveness of answers to questions asked to an LLM-based cybersecurity assistant. Beyond accuracy, we focus on the understandability, actionability and, most importantly, motivating power of answers, given how often users fail to follow cybersecurity recommendations. Specifically, we investigate four personalization strategies, ranging from static user profiles to interaction-history-based personalization, using a corpus of 1,045 real-world cybersecurity questions and a 7-day deployment involving 57 participants and 1,066 user questions. Across both a large-scale automated LLM-based evaluation and human evaluation, conversation-based personalization is consistently favored in comparative ratings of perceived helpfulness and likelihood of following security advice. Importantly, the relative trends observed in the LLM-based evaluation align with those obtained from human evaluation, suggesting that LLM-based evaluation can provide a scalable mechanism for comparing personalization strategies before costly user studies. These results indicate that behavior-driven personalization is a promising direction for LLM-powered cybersecurity assistants and highlight the value of combining LLM-based and human evaluation when studying personalized language-model systems.
tldr: This paper studies personalization strategies for LLM-based cybersecurity assistants and finds conversation-history-based personalization improves perceived helpfulness and follow-through.
motivation: Users often fail to follow cybersecurity recommendations, so the authors investigate whether personalization can improve not just accuracy but understandability, actionability, and motivational power of LLM answers.
method: They compare four personalization strategies using 1,045 real-world cybersecurity questions, a 7-day deployment with 57 participants and 1,066 questions, and both automated LLM-based and human evaluations.
result: Conversation-based personalization is consistently favored in comparative ratings of helpfulness and likelihood of following advice, with LLM-based evaluation trends aligning with human evaluation.
conclusion: Behavior-driven personalization is promising for LLM-powered cybersecurity assistants, and combining LLM-based and human evaluation can scalably compare personalization strategies before costly user studies.

title: Co-occurrence-Aware Quadratic Assignment For Local Feature Matching In Simultaneous Localization And Mapping
authors: Yutaka Yamada, Yohei Hamakawa, Yutaro Ishigaki, Masaya Yamasaki, Kosuke Tatsumura
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local feature matching, which associates keypoints in two images as keypoint pairs, is fundamental to Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (Visual SLAM). Nearest Neighbor (NN) search is commonly used for keypoint matching, but it has difficulty selecting correct keypoint pairs when multiple candidates have similar costs. To improve matching accuracy, this paper proposes a keypoint matching method that considers the pairwise co-occurrence of two keypoint pairs. The keypoint matching is formulated as a quadratic assignment problem, which is an NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem, making it difficult to solve quickly on conventional computers. Recently, Ising machines have been developed as computing devices capable of solving hard combinatorial optimization problems. Using a simulated bifurcation based Ising machine, the proposed method improved matching accuracy by approximately 8 percentage points over a conventional method on the HPatches dataset. Furthermore, we integrated the proposed method into ORB-SLAM3, a representative academic Visual SLAM system, and achieved a 3.78-fold improvement in absolute pose error (APE) and a 2.85-fold improvement in relative pose error (RPE) on the KITTI dataset scenes where multiple same shape objects are repeatedly arranged, which are challenging for accurate self-pose estimation by the original ORB-SLAM3.
tldr: The paper proposes a co-occurrence-aware quadratic assignment formulation of local feature matching in Visual SLAM, solved with a simulated-bifurcation Ising machine to improve pose estimation accuracy.
motivation: Nearest-neighbor keypoint matching often fails when multiple candidate correspondences have similar costs, degrading Visual SLAM accuracy in repetitive-structure scenes.
method: Keypoint matching is formulated as a quadratic assignment problem that accounts for pairwise co-occurrence of keypoint pairs, and is solved using a simulated bifurcation based Ising machine (a classical annealing-style optimizer), then integrated into ORB-SLAM3.
result: Matching accuracy improved by roughly 8 percentage points on HPatches, and ORB-SLAM3 showed 3.78x (APE) and 2.85x (RPE) error reduction on challenging KITTI scenes with repeated same-shape objects.
conclusion: Combinatorial-optimization hardware/accelerators can meaningfully boost classical visual SLAM pipelines, but the work is a robotics/computer-vision application with no quantum information or thermodynamics content.

title: Separating Non-redundancy And Chain Length
authors: Joshua Brakensiek, Venkatesan Guruswami, Aaron Putterman
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a constraint satisfaction problem defined by a relation [MATH], its non-redundancy [MATH] is the size of largest instance (as a function of the number [MATH] of variables) for which no constraint is implied by the rest. Its chain length [MATH] is the largest such instance where the constraints can be ordered so that no constraint is implied by the preceding ones. Clearly [MATH] but so far no asymptotic separation was known between these quantities. We exhibit an explicit arity [MATH] relation for which [MATH].
tldr: The paper constructs an explicit constraint satisfaction relation showing an asymptotic separation between non-redundancy and chain length.
motivation: Non-redundancy and chain length are natural measures of constraint redundancy in CSPs, but no asymptotic separation between them was previously known.
method: The authors exhibit an explicit arity-3 or higher relation and analyze its implication structure to prove that non-redundancy strictly exceeds chain length asymptotically.
result: They give an explicit relation for which the non-redundancy is asymptotically larger than the chain length, resolving an open question.
conclusion: The separation shows the two quantities are fundamentally distinct in the asymptotic regime, with implications for CSP complexity and algebra.

title: Equilibria Of Round-Robin: Computational Hardness And Fairness For Few Subadditive Agents
authors: Paul W. Goldberg, Alexandros Hollender, Giannis Tyrovolas
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The round-robin procedure is a simple and well-studied fair division mechanism where agents pick goods in turns. Motivated by draft mechanisms in sports leagues, we investigate strategic behaviour in online round-robin for subadditive agents. This gives rise to an extensive-form game, and we study the computational problem of computing a subgame perfect Nash equilibrium (SPNE). We show that for just two submodular agents, computing an SPNE is [MATH]-hard. Even for the class of [MATH] utilities, which are a special case of submodular utilities, computing an SPNE remains [MATH]-hard for a small number of agents. We complement our computational results with normative results. We show that for just three additive agents, there exist instances where every equilibrium violates EF1. This separates the online and the direct revelation games. On the positive side, we show that for additive agents every equilibrium allocation is proportional up to one good (PROP1) and for two additive agents it is also EF1. Finally, by showing that round-robin is bossy at equilibrium, we prove that the number of equilibrium allocations can be exponential even if agents have lexicographic preferences.
tldr: The paper studies strategic behavior in the online round-robin fair-division mechanism, proving computational hardness of finding subgame perfect Nash equilibria for subadditive agents and deriving fairness guarantees (or violations) of equilibrium allocations.
motivation: Round-robin drafting is widely used in sports leagues and fair division, yet its strategic (game-theoretic) properties under subadditive preferences are poorly understood, motivating an equilibrium analysis of the induced extensive-form game.
method: The authors model online round-robin as an extensive-form game and analyze the complexity of computing a subgame perfect Nash equilibrium, complemented by normative analysis of equilibrium allocations for additive and lexicographic agents.
result: Computing an SPNE is hard even for two submodular agents and remains hard for a small number of agents with additive utilities; every equilibrium can violate EF1 already for three additive agents, and the number of equilibrium allocations can be exponential.
conclusion: The work separates online round-robin from the direct-revelation game, shows positive PROP1 (and two-agent EF1) guarantees, and establishes that round-robin is bossy at equilibrium, highlighting computational and fairness limitations.

title: The Illusion Of Local Privacy: Confidentiality Boundary Failures In Consumer Llm Serving Systems
authors: Youssef Hamdi Zafan Ibrahim, Muhammad Ikram, Mohammed Khalaf Salama
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Running large language models (LLMs) locally is often considered more private than cloud-hosted inference because user prompts remain on the device. We ask whether keeping inference local is, by itself, sufficient to keep those prompts confidential. Our results show that it is not: prompt confidentiality also depends on how the surrounding serving software handles prompt data before, during, and after inference. We examine four boundaries at which prompt confidentiality can fail in consumer local-LLM serving systems: model loading, runtime memory, wrapper-level persistence, and the serving interface. To study these boundaries, we develop LLAnalyzer, a measurement framework that tests each boundary separately and traces observed failures to the responsible software component. Applying LLAnalyzer to four open-weight model families and two consumer deployment platforms, we find markedly different behaviour across boundaries. In a 24-hour AFL++ campaign with more than 12 million executions, we observe no parser crashes or successful malformed GGUF loads within the explored state space. Runtime memory tells a different story: we recover prompts after inference because multiple plaintext representations survive in allocator-managed memory, and sanitisation reduces this residue without eliminating it. We also find that consumer wrappers can extend prompt lifetime through plaintext persistence. At the serving boundary, we uncover a previously undocumented authorization flaw in llama.cpp that allows one authenticated client to restore another tenant's saved conversation state; the attack succeeds in 200/200 controlled trials. Separately, shared prompt-prefix caching exposes a remote timing oracle that remains distinguishable under WAN conditions. We argue that local LLM systems need explicit guarantees for prompt lifetime, persistent storage, and tenant isolation.
tldr: Local LLM inference is not sufficient for prompt confidentiality because serving software leaks prompt data across model-loading, memory, wrapper-persistence, and serving-interface boundaries.
motivation: Users assume running large language models locally keeps their prompts private since data never leaves the device, but the surrounding serving stack may persist, expose, or leak prompt data regardless of where inference runs.
method: The authors build LLAnalyzer, a measurement framework that tests four confidentiality boundaries separately, and apply it to four open-weight model families and two consumer deployment platforms, including a 24-hour AFL++ fuzzing campaign with over 12 million executions.
result: No parser crashes or malformed GGUF loads were found, but plaintext prompt residue survives in allocator-managed memory even after sanitisation, wrappers extend prompt lifetime via persistence, and a previously undocumented authorization flaw in llama.cpp lets one client restore another tenant's conversation state in 200/200 trials; shared prompt-prefix caching also leaks a remote timing oracle.
conclusion: Local LLM deployment does not by itself guarantee prompt confidentiality, and the authors argue that these systems need explicit guarantees for prompt lifetime, persistent storage, and tenant isolation.

title: A Security Risk Assessment Framework For AI-Powered Development Tools
authors: Salem Aljanah
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI-powered development tools are now widely used to generate code and assist developers with routine programming tasks. Although existing work has identified vulnerabilities in AI-generated code, security-oriented work is often focused on vulnerability detection rather than risk assessment. To address this gap, this paper presents a Security Risk Assessment Framework (SRF) to evaluate the security risks of AI-generated code. SRF combines threat modeling, security analysis, and a quantitative risk evaluation approach based on vulnerability criticality. The framework is applied to a set of security-relevant programming tasks, where code generated by multiple AI-powered development tools is analyzed using Bandit and Semgrep. The results show that AI-generated code can introduce security vulnerabilities across all evaluated tools. They also show that risk levels vary by task type, as input processing and file handling tasks showed higher risk, while simpler tasks remained low-risk. Differences between tools exist but are smaller than differences across task categories. Overall, SRF enables reproducible evaluation of AI-generated code and provides a practical framework for assessing its security implications.
tldr: The paper proposes a Security Risk Assessment Framework (SRF) for quantitatively evaluating the security risks of code generated by AI-powered development tools.
motivation: AI-powered development tools are widely used, yet existing security work focuses on vulnerability detection rather than systematic risk assessment of AI-generated code.
method: SRF combines threat modeling, static security analysis using Bandit and Semgrep, and a quantitative risk evaluation based on vulnerability criticality, applied to a set of security-relevant programming tasks generated by multiple AI tools.
result: AI-generated code introduced vulnerabilities across all evaluated tools, with risk levels varying by task type (input processing and file handling tasks showed higher risk than simpler tasks) and with smaller differences across tools than across task categories.
conclusion: SRF enables reproducible evaluation of AI-generated code and offers a practical framework for assessing its security implications in software development.

title: A Structural Proof Of The Lower Bound 21 For $3\times3$ Matrix Multiplication Over $\mathbb F_2$
authors: Shuxing Yang, Rui Zhao, Junyao Wu, Yize Wang, Wenhao Li, Fujia Chen, Taowen Deng, Shenzhan Hong, Yaqi Li, Zichen Li, Jincheng Mi, Yuang Pan, Kaihao Zhu, Junjie Yang, Hongsheng Chen, Yihao Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the tensor rank of [MATH] matrix multiplication over [MATH] is at least [MATH]. The structural proof, independently developed by Qiushi Engine, converts occupation constraints on a single tensor factor into algebraic relations coupling all three factors. Certified quotient-rank bounds and finite geometry force any hypothetical [MATH]-term decomposition to have first-factor matrix-rank profile [MATH]. The ranks of the corresponding split-flattened summands therefore sum to [MATH], exactly the rank of the full split flattening. Equality in rank subadditivity forces their images to form a direct sum; normalization by the inverse flattening then makes the summands pairwise annihilating idempotents. An explicit product identity for matrix multiplication implies that at most one first factor can be invertible, contradicting the three forced by the profile. The same obstruction constrains [MATH]-term decompositions attaining the split-rank bound. The complete proof, including the finite quotient bounds, is formalized in Lean. The accompanying research trajectory records Qiushi Engine's long-horizon autonomous research, from numerical experiments and quotient constructions to the structural proof.
tldr: Proves a lower bound of 21 on the tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over F2 using a structural algebraic proof formalized in Lean.
motivation: Matrix multiplication tensor rank lower bounds are fundamental to algebraic complexity theory and fast matrix multiplication algorithms.
method: Converts occupation constraints on tensor factors into quotient-rank bounds and finite geometry to force a rank profile, then uses split-flattening and idempotent annihilator arguments to derive a contradiction.
result: Establishes that any 21-term decomposition of 3x3 matrix multiplication over F2 is impossible, with the full proof and quotient bounds formalized in Lean.
conclusion: Advances classical algebraic complexity and tensor rank lower bounds, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Second-Best Gains From Trade In Matching Markets
authors: Xiaohui Bei, Bo Li, Wenhao Wu, Shengwei Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study gains from trade (GFT) in two-sided matching markets with independent private types and arbitrary downward-closed feasibility constraints. The second-best benchmark is the maximum expected GFT achievable by a Bayesian incentive compatible, interim individually rational mechanism that is strongly budget balanced at every report profile. These constraints generally preclude attaining the first-best GFT and raise the question of how much efficiency must be lost. We prove that the second-best GFT is at least one half of the first-best GFT in every such matching market. This recovers and generalizes the recent [MATH] guarantee for bilateral trade by Liu et al. (2026) to markets with multiple buyers and sellers and arbitrary downward-closed feasibility constraints. Together with their matching lower bound for bilateral trade, our result establishes a tight worst-case ratio of [MATH] for this general class of matching markets. Our proof builds on the virtual-GFT framework of Br\"ustle et al. (EC 2017) to reduce the problem to a one-parameter Lagrangian. The main step is a geometric, edge-by-edge analysis based on first-best edge-selection regions, combined with a randomized contraction in rank space.
tldr: The paper proves that in two-sided matching markets with private types and downward-closed feasibility constraints, the second-best gains from trade are at least half of the first-best, establishing a tight worst-case ratio.
motivation: Bayesian incentive compatibility, interim individual rationality, and strong budget balance preclude achieving first-best gains from trade in matching markets, raising the question of how much efficiency must be sacrificed.
method: The authors build on the virtual-GFT framework of Brüstle et al. (EC 2017) to reduce the problem to a one-parameter Lagrangian, then perform a geometric edge-by-edge analysis using first-best edge-selection regions with a randomized contraction in rank space.
result: They show the second-best GFT is at least 1/2 of the first-best in every such matching market, recovering and generalizing the bilateral-trade guarantee of Liu et al. (2026) and, combined with their lower bound, establishing a tight worst-case ratio of 1/2.
conclusion: The work settles the worst-case efficiency loss in general matching markets under strong budget balance, providing a tight characterization of the second-best benchmark.

title: Overlap And Topology Shape Synergy In Collective Knowledge Integration
authors: Masato S. Abe Daeseong Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collective discovery often requires the integration of partially overlapping knowledge, yet the beneficial level of overlap and the role of background topology remain unclear. We model individual knowledge as connected subnetworks of a common knowledge space and distinguish internal synergy, in which integration shortens paths between concepts, from external synergy, in which an unknown concept connects to the shared and all individual-specific regions. Internal synergy peaked at intermediate overlap across random, scale-free, modular, and small-world backgrounds, reflecting a balance between complementarity and common ground. External synergy was strongly topology dependent and was most pronounced when small-world structure maintained overlapping local boundaries. Rewiring separated the total supply of synergistic nodes from their concentration at the accessible boundary; moderate rewiring could increase structural opportunities while dispersing them among more external alternatives and reducing their discovery. Group-size effects on internal synergy depended on topology, whereas strict higher-order external synergy declined as its all-region criterion became more restrictive. Collective discovery therefore depends jointly on knowledge overlap and on how complementary knowledge regions are organized within the surrounding knowledge space.
tldr: A network-science model of collective discovery shows that intermediate knowledge overlap maximizes internal synergy across diverse topologies, while external synergy depends strongly on whether small-world structure maintains overlapping local boundaries.
motivation: Collective discovery requires integrating partially overlapping knowledge, but the optimal degree of overlap and the influence of the surrounding knowledge-space topology are poorly understood.
method: Individual knowledge is modeled as connected subnetworks of a common knowledge space, and internal synergy (path shortening between concepts) is distinguished from external synergy (connection of unknown concepts to shared and individual-specific regions), then studied across random, scale-free, modular, and small-world backgrounds with rewiring and group-size variations.
result: Internal synergy peaks at intermediate overlap for all four topologies, while external synergy is strongly topology dependent and maximal when small-world structure preserves overlapping local boundaries; moderate rewiring can increase structural opportunity while dispersing it and reducing discovery.
conclusion: Collective discovery depends jointly on knowledge overlap and on how complementary knowledge regions are organized within the surrounding knowledge space, with group-size effects being topology dependent.

title: Canonical And Symplectic Analysis Of The Holst Action In The $G\rightarrow 0$ Limit
authors: Victor Julian P\'erez-Aquino (puebla U., Inst. Fis.), Alberto Escalante
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By using the Dirac and symplectic formalisms, the analysis of the Holst action in the [MATH] limit is performed. We study the theory's full canonical structure and symmetries. In particular, we focus on the cases [MATH] and [MATH], aiming to obtain Smolin's auto-self-dual model in terms of the Ashtekar variables and a Barbero-type formulation. We then perform the symplectic analysis and discuss the principal insight of these formalisms.
tldr: The paper performs a canonical and symplectic analysis of the Holst action in the G→0 limit, aiming to recover Smolin's auto-self-dual model in Ashtekar variables and a Barbero-type formulation.
motivation: The Holst action is central to loop quantum gravity, and understanding its canonical structure and symmetries in the G→0 limit may clarify connections to self-dual and Barbero-type formulations.
method: The authors apply the Dirac and symplectic formalisms to analyze the full canonical structure and symmetries of the Holst action in the G→0 limit, focusing on specific parameter cases.
result: They obtain a formulation that yields Smolin's auto-self-dual model in terms of Ashtekar variables and a Barbero-type formulation, while the symplectic analysis provides additional insights into the constraints.
conclusion: The work contributes to the canonical quantization program of gravity and clarifies the relation between different variables in the G→0 limit, but it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimal Resource Extraction Under Distribution Learning And Infinite-Horizon Stochastic Hamilton--Jacobi Equations
authors: Ulrich Horst, Jinniao Qiu, Yang Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an infinite-horizon stochastic control problem for the optimal exploitation of an exhaustible resource with unknown total reserves. Information is generated both endogenously through continued extraction without depletion and exogenously through an external information flow. This interaction makes the natural problem non-Markovian and time-inconsistent. We show that it nevertheless admits an equivalent time-consistent formulation with the same optimal controls. The associated value function is characterized as the unique viscosity solution of a stochastic Hamilton--Jacobi equation with random coefficients. We prove comparison on the infinite horizon through a Snell-envelope-based strict-contact argument and establish uniqueness by an independent Brownian regularization and a BSDE correction, avoiding piecewise Markovian approximations. Finally, we identify the deterministic benchmark and show that, under persistent reserve uncertainty, the rescaled stochastic value function converges to a pathwise deterministic control problem, with the long-run optimal extraction rate determined by the asymptotic hazard rate of the limiting reserve distribution.
tldr: The paper studies optimal extraction of an exhaustible resource with unknown reserves using infinite-horizon stochastic Hamilton–Jacobi equations and distribution learning.
motivation: The problem is motivated by resource economics where information about total reserves is generated through extraction and external information flow, making the natural control problem non-Markovian and time-inconsistent.
method: The authors derive an equivalent time-consistent formulation and characterize the value function as the unique viscosity solution of a stochastic Hamilton–Jacobi equation with random coefficients, using a Snell-envelope-based strict-contact argument and Brownian regularization with a BSDE correction.
result: They establish comparison and uniqueness results on the infinite horizon and show that under persistent reserve uncertainty the rescaled stochastic value function converges to a pathwise deterministic control problem with a long-run optimal extraction rate tied to the asymptotic hazard rate.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous stochastic control framework for optimal resource extraction under learning, but it lies outside quantum information theory, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Random Tilts To Find Stationary Points In Stochastic Convex Optimization
authors: Felipe Areces, John C. Duchi, Malo Sommers
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of finding stationary points of stochastic convex functions and related variational inequalities. For each, we show that regularized empirical risk minimization, coupled with a random tilting perturbation, obtains stationarity residual order [MATH] for [MATH]-dimensional problems given [MATH] observations. We present a few complementary results that show that some dimension dependence is necessary, in distinction from standard stochastic optimization and empirical risk minimization, by providing minimax lower bounds scaling as [MATH].
tldr: The paper shows that regularized empirical risk minimization with random tilting perturbations achieves optimal stationarity residuals for stochastic convex optimization, with matching minimax lower bounds establishing necessary dimension dependence.
motivation: Finding stationary points of stochastic convex functions and variational inequalities typically achieves dimension-independent rates in standard stochastic optimization, so the authors ask whether the same holds for stationarity residuals rather than function-value suboptimality.
method: They analyze regularized empirical risk minimization combined with a random tilting perturbation, proving upper bounds on stationarity residual for d-dimensional problems with n observations, and complement these with minimax lower bounds.
result: The proposed random-tilt scheme attains stationarity residual of a certain order, and the minimax lower bounds show that some dimension dependence is unavoidable, in contrast to standard stochastic optimization and ERM.
conclusion: Random tilting provides an optimal approach to finding stationary points in stochastic convex optimization and variational inequalities, with fundamental dimension-dependent limits that distinguish this setting from classical ERM.

title: Hypercyclicity And Lipschitz-free Operators
authors: Christian Cobollo, Romuald Ernst, Quentin Menet, Alfred Peris
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study linearizations of dynamical systems and some of its topological properties. Special attention is paid to the case of Lipschitz-free operators, and they are shown to model the dynamics of very general linearizations. We provide a new criterion, called the targeting property, for the (weakly) mixing property in a linear dynamical system through a (possibly) non-linear restriction of it. We then apply this criterion to the linearization [MATH] of a Lipschitz map [MATH], where [MATH] is a metric space and the operator [MATH] is defined on the corresponding Lipschitz-free space [MATH]---the so-called Lipschitz-free operators. We show that, under some natural assumptions on the distance considered in [MATH], the operator [MATH] is hypercyclic if and only if the map [MATH] has the targeting property.
tldr: The paper introduces a 'targeting property' criterion for (weakly) mixing linear dynamical systems and applies it to characterize hypercyclicity of Lipschitz-free operators arising from linearizations of Lipschitz maps on metric spaces.
motivation: Linearizations of nonlinear dynamical systems are a central tool in topological dynamics, and Lipschitz-free spaces provide a natural functional-analytic framework for such linearizations; the authors aim to give sharp criteria for chaotic-type behavior of these operators.
method: The authors develop a new sufficient criterion, the targeting property, for (weakly) mixing of linear dynamical systems via a possibly nonlinear restriction, and then apply it to the linearization operator on the Lipschitz-free space associated with a Lipschitz map.
result: Under natural assumptions on the metric, the Lipschitz-free operator is shown to be hypercyclic if and only if the underlying Lipschitz map enjoys the targeting property.
conclusion: Lipschitz-free operators faithfully model the dynamics of very general linearizations, and the targeting property offers a versatile tool for establishing (weak) mixing and hypercyclicity.

title: A Geometric View Of Adaptive Cross Approximation Via Exterior Algebra
authors: Trevor Loe, Longxiu Huang, Deanna Needell
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive cross approximation (ACA) constructs low-rank CUR approximations from selected rows and columns of a matrix, making it attractive when individual entries are inexpensive to query but forming or repeatedly multiplying by the full matrix is not. Its practical performance, however, is not well explained by existing worst-case bounds, which can be exponentially large and often fail to predict when greedy largest-entry pivoting performs poorly. By viewing the matrix as a cross-gram matrix, we reinterpret the classical determinantal formula for the CUR residual through the lens of exterior algebra. In this representation, each residual entry is a weighted inner product between two [MATH]-blades divided by the normalized volume of the pivot block. The formula separates three effects: the weighted magnitudes of singular-vector rows, their angular geometry, and the conditioning of the selected pivots. From this we recover a classical [MATH]-type estimate, characterize when one pivot annihilates or nearly annihilates additional rows and columns, obtain a quasi-optimality estimate for positive-semidefinite matrices, and bound the rank-one update through an explicit angle-based formula. We use this framework to explain the failure of greedy ACA on an asymmetric spiral-kernel example and to motivate a geometry-aware weighted-mass pivoting rule for radial-basis Galerkin stiffness matrices. In the reported experiments, weighted-mass pivoting often reduces the Frobenius residual relative to greedy pivoting and randomly pivoted Cholesky while retaining comparable runtime on parallel hardware.
tldr: The paper reinterprets adaptive cross approximation (ACA) low-rank CUR residuals through exterior algebra, yielding a geometric decomposition that explains pivot-selection behavior and motivates a weighted-mass pivoting rule.
motivation: Existing worst-case bounds for ACA are exponentially loose and fail to predict when greedy largest-entry pivoting performs poorly, leaving practical performance unexplained.
method: The matrix is viewed as a cross-gram matrix, and the classical determinantal formula for the CUR residual is recast in exterior algebra as a weighted inner product of two blades divided by the normalized pivot-block volume.
result: The reformulation yields a classical-type estimate, conditions under which a pivot annihilates additional rows/columns, a quasi-optimality bound for positive-semidefinite matrices, and an explicit angle-based rank-one update bound, explaining greedy ACA failure on an asymmetric spiral kernel.
conclusion: A geometry-aware weighted-mass pivoting rule is proposed, which in experiments often lowers the Frobenius residual versus greedy pivoting and randomly pivoted Cholesky at comparable runtime.

title: Structure Properties Of Banach Spaces Of I-null Sequences
authors: Michael A. Rinc\'on-Villamizar, Victor S. Ronchim, Carlos Uzc\'ategui Aylwin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate structural properties of the ideal-null sequence spaces c_{0,I} and c_{0,I}(X), and of the quotient l_infty/c_{0,I}, emphasizing the interaction between Banach space theory and combinatorial, topological, and measure-theoretic properties of the underlying ideal. We study classical problems related to c_0, including the dual space, compactness criteria, bounded and compact c_{0,I}-valued operators, Sobczyk-type extension phenomena, and complemented copies of c_0. We identify c_{0,I}^* isometrically with a space of bounded finitely additive measures on I and obtain a canonical atomic-singular decomposition, with l_1 as an isometrically complemented summand. A Dini principle for ideal convergence yields characterizations of relatively compact subsets of c_{0,I} and of compact operators with range in c_{0,I}. We prove a Sobczyk theorem for c_{0,I} and show that its separable-injectivity constant is exactly 2 for every proper ideal. We also construct, in ZFC, a class of statistical ideals for which c_{0,I} is not complemented in l_infty, and characterize complemented copies of c_0 in c_{0,I}(X) via the corresponding properties of c_{0,I} and X. Finally, we describe quotients associated with direct and Frolik sums of ideals, characterize Banach-lattice copies of c_0(kappa) in l_infty/c_{0,I} through I-almost disjoint families, identify ad(I) with the cellularity of the associated Stone space, and determine its behavior under Fubini products.
tldr: A pure functional-analysis study of the structural properties of ideal-null sequence Banach spaces c_{0,I} and c_{0,I}(X) and of the quotient l_infty/c_{0,I}.
motivation: The authors aim to extend classical Banach-space results about c_0 (duality, compactness, Sobczyk extension, complemented copies) to the setting of sequence spaces defined by a combinatorial ideal I.
method: Classical Banach space techniques—isometric dual identifications with finitely additive measures, Dini-type principles for ideal convergence, ZFC constructions of statistical ideals, and Stone-space / lattice-theoretic analysis.
result: They identify c_{0,I}^* with a space of bounded finitely additive measures on I, prove a Sobczyk theorem with separable-injectivity constant exactly 2, construct ideals for which c_{0,I} is not complemented in l_infty, and characterize Banach-lattice copies of c_0(kappa) in l_infty/c_{0,I} via I-almost disjoint families.
conclusion: The work deepens the interplay between Banach space theory and the combinatorial, topological, and measure-theoretic structure of ideals, with no bearing on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Bounded Chaining In Measurable Dynamics
authors: Jenna Zomback Anush Tserunyan
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a one-parameter family of notions between double ergodicity and metric ergodicity for measure-class preserving (i.e., nonsingular) actions of countable groups on standard probability spaces, providing infinitely many new invariants distinguishing weakly mixing actions. We call these properties (essentially) [MATH]-chaining, for [MATH]. We apply this framework to study boundary actions of free groups of finite rank [MATH], where the boundary is equipped with a stationary Markov measure. We prove that in this context, weak mixing is equivalent to [MATH]-chaining, as well as to strict irreducibility of the transition matrix of the Markov measure.
tldr: Introduces bounded chaining invariants for measure-class preserving group actions, distinguishing weakly mixing actions, and applies them to boundary actions of free groups with stationary Markov measures.
motivation: To provide new invariants between double ergodicity and metric ergodicity for nonsingular actions of countable groups.
method: Defines a one-parameter family of M-chaining properties and studies boundary actions of finite-rank free groups equipped with stationary Markov measures.
result: In this setting, weak mixing is equivalent to M-chaining and to strict irreducibility of the transition matrix of the Markov measure.
conclusion: The framework yields infinitely many new invariants and connects ergodic properties of group actions to Markov chain irreducibility.

title: Sample Average Approximation Of Multiobjective Stochastic Optimization Problems With Application In Insurance
authors: Bogdan Norkin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The article describes a technique for solving multiobjective stochastic optimization problems. As a generalized model of a stochastic system to be optimized a vector (input-random output) system is used. Ran- dom outputs are converted into a vector of deterministic performance and risk indicators. The problem is to find those inputs that correspond to a Pareto-optimal values of output indicators. The problem is approximated by a sequence of deterministic multi-criteria optimization problems, where, for example, the objective vector function is a sample average approximation of the original one and the feasible set is a discrete sample approximation of the feasible inputs. Approximate optimal solutions are defined as weakly Pareto-efficient ones within some vector tolerance. Convergence analysis includes establishing convergence of the general approx- imation scheme and establishing conditions of convergence with probability one under proper regulation of sampling parameters. The proposed technique is illustrated on a computer system for supporting multi-criteria optimization of insurance business.
tldr: The paper develops a sample average approximation technique for solving multiobjective stochastic optimization problems, illustrated with an insurance business application.
motivation: Multiobjective stochastic optimization problems are difficult to solve exactly because the objective involves random outputs, motivating tractable deterministic approximation schemes.
method: Random outputs are converted into vectors of deterministic performance and risk indicators, and the problem is approximated by a sequence of deterministic multi-criteria optimizations using sample average approximations of the objective and a discrete sample approximation of the feasible set.
result: Convergence of the general approximation scheme is established, along with conditions for convergence with probability one under proper regulation of sampling parameters, with weakly Pareto-efficient solutions defined up to vector tolerance.
conclusion: The technique provides a rigorous and practical framework for multiobjective stochastic optimization, demonstrated on a computer system supporting multi-criteria optimization of insurance business decisions.

title: Existence And Regularity Of Stable Resonant Spectral Submanifolds And Linearization Maps
authors: Rafael de la Llave Florian Kogelbauer
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of [MATH]-regular stable invariant manifolds and linear conjugacies for analytic maps near a hyperbolic fixed point in the presence of resonances. The regularity exponent [MATH] depends on the minimal resonant index, while the H\"older exponent can be chosen arbitrarily close to [MATH], i.e., [MATH] for any [MATH]. As a consequence, we obtain the stable version of the Hartman conjecture for analytic systems with semisimple linearization: in the fully stable case the local conjugacy can be chosen [MATH] for every [MATH].\\ Our approach introduces a new class of functional expansions based on logarithmic polynomials, which enables the invariance equation to be solved explicitly and algorithmically to arbitrary order. The existence results are obtained via a fixed-point argument in a suitable Banach space. We further present several analytic examples that both illustrate the applicability of the theorem while demonstrating the necessity of its assumptions.
tldr: The paper proves existence and regularity of stable invariant manifolds and linearizing conjugacies for analytic maps near hyperbolic fixed points with resonances, including a stable version of the Hartman conjecture.
motivation: The Hartman conjecture and the regularity of conjugacies to linearizations in the presence of resonances are long-standing problems in dynamical systems, and the authors aim to establish sharp regularity results for stable manifolds.
method: They introduce functional expansions based on logarithmic polynomials to solve the invariance equation explicitly and use a fixed-point argument in a suitable Banach space.
result: They obtain C^r-regular stable invariant manifolds and Hölder linear conjugacies with exponents arbitrarily close to a bound determined by the minimal resonant index, yielding the stable Hartman conjecture for semisimple linearization.
conclusion: The results extend linearization theory for resonant analytic systems and are illustrated by analytic examples that also show the necessity of the assumptions.

title: Bounded Cubic Integer Programming In Fixed Dimension
authors: Robert Hildebrand Cinar Ari
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the exact minimization of a rational cubic polynomial over the integer points of a rational polytope in fixed dimension. Del Pia, Hildebrand, Weismantel, and Zemmer proved polynomial-time solvability in dimension two, while quartic polynomial minimization is already NP-hard in dimension two. We show that the bounded cubic result extends to every fixed dimension. The proof combines two exact identities for cubic polynomials with three ingredients from the recent fixed-dimensional algorithms for integer quadratic programming of Ari and Hildebrand: symmetric displacement covers, negative-displacement search for quadratic forms, and integer-query convex feasibility. At an integer query point, a negative Hessian direction yields a linear curvature cut valid for every global minimizer in the current cell, while absence of such a direction yields a linear objective cut through an exact endpoint-Hessian identity. These cuts define an integer-query separation oracle for the convex hull of the curvature-admissible sublevel points. Integer convex feasibility via ellipsoids and lattice algorithms then gives exact optimization without computing lattice centerpoints. A real-algebraic localization bound extends the result to unbounded polyhedra with a bounded real improving sublevel, including all coercive objectives. The argument also explains why degree three is a natural boundary for this approach: the symmetric second difference of a cubic is exactly its directional Hessian, which is affine in the basepoint; for quartics an additional fourth-order term appears.
tldr: The paper proves that exact minimization of a bounded cubic polynomial over integer points of a rational polytope is polynomial-time solvable in every fixed dimension.
motivation: Previous work showed polynomial-time solvability for cubic objectives in dimension two, while quartic minimization is NP-hard even in dimension two, leaving open whether the bounded cubic result extends to all fixed dimensions.
method: The proof combines exact algebraic identities for cubic polynomials with fixed-dimensional integer quadratic programming techniques, including symmetric displacement covers, negative-displacement search, and an integer-query separation oracle built from curvature and objective cuts.
result: The paper establishes polynomial-time solvability of bounded cubic integer programming in any fixed dimension, and extends the result to unbounded polyhedra with a bounded real improving sublevel via a real-algebraic localization bound.
conclusion: Degree three is a natural boundary for this approach because the symmetric second difference of a cubic equals its directional Hessian, whereas quartics introduce an additional fourth-order term.

title: A Continuous-time Dynamic Contracting Problem With Limited Liability And Finite Horizon
authors: Andrea Bovo, Tiziano de Angelis, St\'{e}phane Villeneuve
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We perform a detailed study of a principal--agent problem in a continuous time version of the celebrated Holmstr\"om--Milgrom model (Econometrica 55 (2), 1987) where we add limited liability for the Agent. We develop a probabilistic methodology to prove that the Principal's value function is the unique bounded classical solution to a fully nonlinear and fully degenerate partial differential equation (PDE) with Cauchy-Dirichlet boundary conditions on [MATH]. Indeed, we also prove infinite continuous differentiability of the solution in the interior of the domain. The strength of our regularity result is such that we can ensure existence of optimal controls in strong form---a rare occurrence in dynamic contracting---and we obtain fine properties of the optimal control map, including a characterisation via a further nonlinear degenerate PDE.
tldr: The paper studies a continuous-time principal-agent contracting problem with limited liability and finite horizon, proving regularity of the Principal's value function and existence of optimal controls.
motivation: The work extends the Holmström-Milgrom dynamic contracting model by adding limited liability for the agent, aiming to characterize optimal contracts in a finite-horizon continuous-time setting.
method: The authors use a probabilistic methodology to show that the Principal's value function is the unique bounded classical solution to a fully nonlinear, fully degenerate PDE with Cauchy-Dirichlet boundary conditions, and prove infinite continuous differentiability in the interior.
result: They establish existence of optimal controls in strong form, a rare result in dynamic contracting, and characterize the optimal control map via a further nonlinear degenerate PDE.
conclusion: The paper provides a rigorous mathematical treatment of a continuous-time contracting problem with limited liability, contributing to dynamic contract theory rather than quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Predictive Online Disturbance-Action Control For Linear Dynamical Systems
authors: Xia Jiang, Jianping Li, Lihua Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies predictive online control for linear dynamical systems with time-varying cost functions, motivated by applications such as real-time adaptive control of motorized LiDAR sensing systems, where the controller must adjust the sensing direction online to balance localization accuracy, scanning efficiency, and smooth actuation under changing environmental conditions. We propose a predictive online control (POC) algorithm that leverages short-term predictions of future cost functions while accounting for the memory effect induced by system dynamics. Using the disturbance-action controller (DAC) parameterization, the online control problem is transformed into an OCO-with-memory formulation over policy parameters. We develop a windowed receding-horizon update that incorporates short-term predictions and accommodates a total-variation regularizer to suppress abrupt policy variations. Theoretically, we prove that POC achieves a dynamic policy regret bound scaling with the path length of the comparator sequence, and provide sufficient conditions in terms of logarithmic prediction and memory horizons for the regret guarantee. The proposed method is evaluated on a motorized LiDAR sensing task, demonstrating improved localization accuracy together with a favorable trade-off between sensing accuracy and scanning completeness.
tldr: The paper proposes a predictive online control (POC) algorithm for linear dynamical systems with time-varying costs, using disturbance-action control and online convex optimization with memory to achieve dynamic policy regret bounds.
motivation: Real-time adaptive control tasks such as motorized LiDAR sensing require controllers to balance accuracy, efficiency, and smooth actuation under changing conditions, motivating predictive online control with short-term cost forecasts.
method: The authors parameterize policies via disturbance-action control (DAC), recasting online control as OCO-with-memory over policy parameters, and develop a windowed receding-horizon update with a total-variation regularizer on top of short-term predictions.
result: They prove a dynamic policy regret bound scaling with the comparator path length, give sufficient conditions on logarithmic prediction and memory horizons, and demonstrate improved LiDAR localization accuracy with a favorable accuracy-completeness trade-off.
conclusion: Predictive online control with memory-aware DAC parameterization yields provable regret guarantees and practical gains, though the work sits entirely in classical control/optimization rather than quantum information science.

title: Estimate Then Predict: Convex Formulation For Travel Demand Forecasting
authors: Youngseo Kim, Gioele Zardini, Samitha Samaranayake, Soroosh Shafiee
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Travel demand forecasting is essential for evaluating large-scale infrastructure projects, yet the traditional sequential four-step process can produce inconsistencies across trip distribution, mode choice, and traffic assignment. Although combined models address these inconsistencies, their practical use has been limited by simplified behavioral assumptions, computational burden, and the lack of a unified parameter-estimation framework. We propose a convex programming approach that integrates destination, mode, and route choices within a hierarchical extended logit model. The optimal primal solution characterizes the joint travel-demand equilibrium, while the optimal dual variables recover taste coefficients, alternative-specific constants, and destination- and mode-level scale parameters. The model captures mode correlations through nested logit and route overlap through path-size logit. Its convex structure provides global optimality guarantees and enables efficient solution using off-the-shelf conic solvers. Observed travel patterns are incorporated through moment and conditional-entropy constraints, while the route-level dispersion parameter is calibrated separately using partial link counts. Numerical experiments on eight benchmark networks demonstrate the scalability and computational efficiency of the formulation.
tldr: The paper proposes a convex programming formulation for travel demand forecasting that jointly models destination, mode, and route choices with global optimality guarantees.
motivation: Traditional sequential travel demand models can yield inconsistencies, while combined models are often computationally burdensome and rely on simplified behavioral assumptions.
method: The authors integrate destination, mode, and route choices in a hierarchical extended logit model using convex programming, with primal optimality characterizing equilibrium and dual variables recovering model parameters.
result: Numerical experiments on eight benchmark networks demonstrate scalability and computational efficiency using off-the-shelf conic solvers.
conclusion: The convex formulation provides a unified, globally optimal framework for travel demand forecasting, incorporating observed travel patterns via moment and entropy constraints.

title: "Your Robot Was Trained On A Lie": Collision Mesh Poisoning Attacks On Robotic Manipulation
authors: Gengyang Xu, Dongwei Xiao, Yiteng Peng, Yanbo Dai, Ruochen Zhou, Shing-Chi Cheung, Xiaoyu Ji, Wenyuan Xu, Shuai Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning-enabled robotic manipulation increasingly relies on robot simulators for policy training and evaluation before real-world deployment. Inside a simulator, a 3D asset contains two separate geometries: a visual mesh used for rendering and a collision mesh used for physical interaction. For computational efficiency, the collision mesh is deliberately a coarse approximation that need not have the same geometry as the visual mesh, a legitimate and pervasive discrepancy we call the Visual--Collision Gap (V--C Gap). We show that the V--C Gap opens a new and practical attack surface, and propose Collision Mesh Poisoning (CMP), the first poisoning attack against robotic manipulation delivered through the 3D asset supply chain. An attacker modifies only the collision mesh of a 3D asset, leaving the visual mesh and all other components unchanged. A policy trained and evaluated with the poisoned asset behaves normally throughout simulation, yet degrades, fails, or creates physical safety risks once deployed in the real world. Since current asset review practices cover malware, copyright, and format compliance, but not visual--collision consistency, poisoned assets can be distributed through legitimate supply chain channels. We evaluate several defenses and our results show that they are insufficient to defend against CMP, highlighting the need for new defenses.
tldr: The paper introduces Collision Mesh Poisoning (CMP), the first poisoning attack against learning-enabled robotic manipulation that exploits the discrepancy between visual and collision meshes in 3D simulation assets.
motivation: Robot simulators are widely used for policy training and evaluation, and 3D assets legitimately contain a coarse collision mesh that differs from the visual mesh (the Visual-Collision Gap), creating an unchecked attack surface in the asset supply chain.
method: An attacker modifies only the collision mesh of a 3D asset, leaving the visual mesh unchanged, so that policies trained and evaluated in simulation appear normal but degrade or create safety risks when deployed on real hardware; several existing defenses are evaluated against the attack.
result: Poisoned assets pass current review practices (malware, copyright, format compliance) and can be distributed through legitimate supply-chain channels, while evaluated defenses prove insufficient to detect or mitigate CMP.
conclusion: The Visual-Collision Gap constitutes a new and practical security threat for robotic manipulation, highlighting the need for new defenses that verify visual-collision consistency in 3D assets.

title: Isia-af: Orchestrating Reproducible Attacks And Multi-Source Data Collection For Ot Systems
authors: Stefan Manfred Haratzm\"uller, Thomas Rosenstatter, Olaf Sa{\ss}nick, Dalibor Sain, Stefan Huber
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operational Technology (OT) environments require realistic, reproducible security datasets, yet existing approaches often lack automation, multi-source data capture, and sufficient documentation for reuse. This paper presents ISIA-AF, a modular attack framework for orchestrating reproducible attack execution and automated dataset generation on industrial systems. The framework coordinates distributed attack clients, records network traffic and operational data, ultimately leading to a multi-source dataset. We derive functional and non-functional requirements from prior work and stakeholder discussions, and realise the framework following a design science research approach. A case study on the ISIA testbed, comprising a real industrial system and a simulated process, demonstrates how the framework supports centralised control, low communication overhead, and flexible deployment across network segments. The result is a practical basis for generating extensible, multi-source OT security datasets for intrusion detection research.
tldr: ISIA-AF is a modular framework for orchestrating reproducible attack execution and automated multi-source dataset generation in operational technology (OT) industrial systems.
motivation: OT environments need realistic, reproducible security datasets for intrusion detection research, but existing approaches lack automation, multi-source capture, and documentation for reuse.
method: The authors derive functional and non-functional requirements from prior work and stakeholder discussions, then build the framework using a design science research approach, validated via a case study on the ISIA testbed combining a real industrial system with a simulated process.
result: The framework enables centralised control of distributed attack clients, network and operational data recording, low communication overhead, and flexible deployment across network segments, yielding an extensible multi-source OT security dataset.
conclusion: ISIA-AF provides a practical basis for generating reproducible, multi-source OT security datasets, supporting future intrusion detection research on industrial control systems.

title: Detecting Logic Vulnerabilities Across The Contract And Device Layers Of Blockchain-Enabled IoT With Multi-Agent Heterogeneous Graph Attention
authors: Minfeng Qi, Jialin Li, Tianqing Zhu, Lefeng Zhang, Zhe Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blockchain-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) systems integrate smart contracts with embedded devices to support decentralized device management and access control. Their security therefore depends jointly on the logic of on-chain contracts and off-chain device firmware. Logic flaws in either layer can violate the same system invariants, such as unauthorized access, improper state changes, or unguarded privileged operations. Existing approaches rely on contract analysis, firmware analysis, and graph-based vulnerability detection. However, these methods typically focus on a single layer or artifact and often depend on predefined vulnerability patterns, emulation fidelity, or homogeneous representations that obscure security-relevant component roles. They also lack a unified architecture that supports different security tasks while remaining deployable on resource-constrained gateways. To address these limitations, we extend MA-HGAT into a cross-layer multi-agent heterogeneous graph attention framework that models contracts, firmware artifacts, device fleets, and transaction streams with a unified four-role, nine-relation schema. Role-aligned agents exchange heterogeneous evidence through cross-attention, while graph-, link-, and node-level heads support multiple detection tasks and a role-based gateway--cloud partition enables lightweight edge inference. MA-HGAT thus provides a unified and deployable framework for detecting logic vulnerabilities across the contract and device layers of blockchain-enabled IoT systems.
tldr: The paper proposes MA-HGAT, a cross-layer multi-agent heterogeneous graph attention framework for detecting logic vulnerabilities spanning smart contracts and device firmware in blockchain-enabled IoT systems.
motivation: Security of blockchain-enabled IoT depends jointly on on-chain contract logic and off-chain device firmware, yet existing vulnerability detection methods focus on a single layer or artifact and rely on predefined patterns, emulation fidelity, or homogeneous graph representations that obscure component roles.
method: The authors extend MA-HGAT into a cross-layer, multi-agent heterogeneous graph attention framework that models contracts, firmware artifacts, device fleets, and transaction streams via a unified four-role, nine-relation schema, with role-aligned agents exchanging evidence through cross-attention and graph-, link-, and node-level heads supporting multiple detection tasks.
result: The framework supports multiple detection tasks in a unified architecture and uses a role-based gateway-cloud partition to enable lightweight inference on resource-constrained edge gateways.
conclusion: MA-HGAT is presented as a unified, deployable framework for detecting logic vulnerabilities across the contract and device layers of blockchain-enabled IoT systems.

title: Echo: Learning-based Matching Decompilation Using Trusted Back Translation
authors: Jun Bi, Xiangxin Fang, Aarsh Chaube, Jos\'e Wesley de Souza Magalh\~aes, Rodrigo C. O. Rocha, Michael O'boyle
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural decompilers can recover readable and recompilable source code from binaries, but their predictions remain difficult to trust. Matching decompilation addresses this problem by searching for source code whose recompiled assembly exactly matches the target, providing stronger evidence of correctness. However, exact matching remains challenging for optimized binaries under unknown compilation configurations. We present Echo, a matching decompilation system based on trusted back-translation. Our key insight is to use compilation not only for verification, but also as trusted feedback to guide iterative search. Echo first uses a domain-specific model to generate candidate programs and compilation configurations. It recompiles these candidates, measures assembly-level similarity, and synthesizes promising code-configuration pairs. Remaining mismatches are then progressively repaired using rule-based rewriting, neural refinement, and reasoning-based refinement. We evaluate Echo on function-level benchmarks and the Mirai malware binary. Compared with the strongest baseline, Echo produces 2.43x more exact matches on average and achieves the highest structural similarity to ground-truth source code. On Mirai, Echo matches 2.75x and 7.4x as many functions as GPT-5.6 and Codex, respectively.
tldr: Echo is a matching decompilation system that uses compilation as trusted feedback to iteratively search for source code whose recompiled assembly exactly matches an optimized binary's target.
motivation: Neural decompilers can produce readable, recompilable code but their outputs are hard to trust; matching decompilation offers stronger correctness evidence, yet exact matching of optimized binaries under unknown compilation configurations remains difficult.
method: Echo generates candidate programs and compilation configurations with a domain-specific model, recompiles them, measures assembly-level similarity, and synthesizes promising code-configuration pairs, then repairs residual mismatches via rule-based rewriting, neural refinement, and reasoning-based refinement.
result: On function-level benchmarks Echo yields 2.43x more exact matches on average than the strongest baseline with the highest structural similarity to ground-truth source; on the Mirai malware binary it matches 2.75x and 7.4x as many functions as GPT-5.6 and Codex respectively.
conclusion: Treating compilation as trusted feedback for iterative search makes matching decompilation markedly more effective on optimized binaries and real-world malware, improving the trustworthiness of binary-to-source recovery.

title: On-Demand Combinatorial Event Markets On Kalshi: Instantiation, Concentration, And Effective Market Breadth
authors: Maksym Nechepurenko
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kalshi's multivariate-event architecture produces market objects on demand from exact selected legs. Across a registered seven-day interval, 190 independently validated temporal shards yield 7,611,594 unique REST MVE market tickers after excluding 5,777 boundary-overlap observations; the population was created at an average rate of 1.087 million objects per day, with strong hourly burstiness. The hierarchy is sharply compressed relative to the market-object count: 5,262,526 exact event keys, three collection keys, 83,701 selected-leg primitives, and 66,344,938 selected-leg occurrences. The largest collection accounts for 7,217,085 objects (94.82 percent), with an effective collection count of 1.11; the effective primitive count is approximately 720. REST and WebSocket are distinct observation surfaces: 1,487,330 created-notification tickers intersect the REST population in only 276,177 exact tickers. All three observed collection keys have current endpoint confirmation without establishing historical collection or rule versions. The exact structural signature yields 7,611,594 unique signatures with zero collision groups. At retrieval, 2,692,787 objects (35.38 percent) have positive cumulative volume or open interest; all observed 24-hour-volume values are zero and trade-count fields are unavailable. This is current-snapshot activity eligibility, not historical trading. The central result is that a very large on-demand market-object population is generated by a concentrated collection layer and reused primitive vocabulary; economic breadth must be measured at several hierarchical levels rather than by ticker count alone. Exact public endpoint evidence is available for 7,357,576 MVE objects, whereas only 126,806 have an exact determination-to-endpoint pair: terminal-state coverage and lifecycle-path coverage are distinct statistical objects.
tldr: The paper analyzes the large-scale, on-demand generation of combinatorial event markets on Kalshi, focusing on market-object counts, concentration, and effective breadth using REST and WebSocket API data.
motivation: The study aims to characterize the structure and economic breadth of Kalshi's multivariate-event (MVE) markets, which can generate millions of unique tickers, and argues that ticker counts alone are misleading.
method: Using a registered seven-day interval with 190 temporal shards, the authors collect and validate REST MVE market tickers, compare them with WebSocket creation notifications, and compute hierarchical counts and coverage statistics.
result: They find 7,611,594 unique REST MVE tickers generated at ~1.087 million objects/day, with 94.82% belonging to a single collection and an effective collection count of only 1.11; only 35.38% of objects have positive volume or open interest at retrieval.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that a highly concentrated collection layer and reused primitive vocabulary underlie the apparent market-object scale, implying that economic breadth must be measured across multiple hierarchical levels rather than by raw ticker count.

title: Activity-induced Emergent Flatness, Instabilities And Pattern Formation In Fluid Membranes
authors: Debayan Jana, Astik Haldar, Abhik Basu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that microscopically inversion-asymmetric, permeable active fluid membranes are statistically flat and effectively inversion-symmetric at large scales. Their fluctuations are governed by an asymptotically exact linear hydrodynamic equation giving orientational long-range order and positional quasi-long-range order. At intermediate scales, their dynamics is described by a Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation with spatially long-range noise, producing rough membranes with short-range translational and long-range orientational order described by exactly known scaling exponents. Active stresses can destabilize the membrane at long wavelengths, while sufficiently strong active permeation flow can drive finite-wavevector instabilities and pattern formation. These results reveal a novel activity-driven route to the destruction of flat fluid membranes.
tldr: Active fluid membranes are shown to exhibit emergent flatness, long-range orientational order, KPZ-like roughening, and activity-driven instabilities and pattern formation.
motivation: Understanding how microscopic activity and inversion asymmetry affect the large-scale statistics and stability of fluid membranes is important in active matter and biological physics.
method: The authors derive an asymptotically exact linear hydrodynamic equation for the membrane fluctuations and analyze intermediate-scale dynamics using a Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation with spatially long-range noise.
result: The membrane is statistically flat with quasi-long-range positional and long-range orientational order at large scales; active stresses cause long-wavelength instabilities, and strong active permeation flow produces finite-wavevector instabilities and patterns.
conclusion: Activity provides a novel route to destroying flat fluid membranes through instabilities and pattern formation, with implications for active membrane physics.

title: An Additional Possibilities Of The Standard Method Of Inverting The Radon Transform
authors: D. S. Anikonov, S. G. Kazantsev, D. S. Konovalova
abstract: ArXiv:2609.17803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The problem of inverting the Radon integral transform in finite-dimensional Euclidean space is considered. The relevance of this topic for probing issues is indicated. It is noted that for the latter direction, it is natural to consider the integrand as discontinuous function. However, the available inversion formulas are only proven for differentiable functions. Therefore, the question of obtaining formulas for discontinuous functions arises. It is set that the required results can be obtained by some modification of available proofs for smooth functions.
tldr: The paper proposes modifications to standard inversion formulas for the Radon transform to handle discontinuous integrands in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
motivation: The Radon transform inversion is relevant to probing problems where the integrand is naturally discontinuous, but existing inversion formulas are only proven for differentiable functions.
method: The authors modify available proofs for smooth functions to obtain inversion formulas applicable to discontinuous functions.
result: New inversion formulas or extensions are derived for the discontinuous case using a modification of the standard proof technique.
conclusion: The work expands the applicability of Radon transform inversion to a broader class of functions relevant to probing applications.

title: MLegS: A Modern Mapped Legendre Spectral Method Solver For Unbounded Domains With Parallelization
authors: Jinge Wang Sangjoon Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: MLegS is an open-source Modern Fortran code package for solving linear and nonlinear time-dependent partial differential equations on radially unbounded domains. It builds on an earlier in-house prototype, recasting it as a modular solver with a unified interface for fields, transforms, and spectral operators. Within this framework, the numerical formulation maps [MATH] onto a finite interval, where associated Legendre functions provide the radial basis, while Fourier series represent the periodic azimuthal and axial directions. The mapped radial basis represents radial infinity without imposing an artificial boundary condition at finite radius while incorporating the regularity required at [MATH] according to azimuthal order. The implementation distributes the corresponding field layouts using the Message-Passing Interface (MPI), with strong- and weak-scaling measurements extending to 512 cores across four compute nodes. Beyond parallel performance, three examples assess the solver across diffusion, reaction-diffusion, and vortex dynamics: closed-form diffusion solutions establish spectral spatial convergence and the design orders of both semi-implicit integrators; a Fisher-Kolmogorov-Petrovsky-Piskunov front matches the linearized solution and propagates at the classical speed within its logarithmic correction; and vortex-pair simulations based on toroidal-poloidal decomposition yield a measured Crow growth rate [MATH] above the theoretical prediction and demonstrate the reconnection of the vortex pair.
tldr: MLegS is an open-source Fortran solver using mapped Legendre spectral methods with MPI parallelization for time-dependent PDEs on radially unbounded domains.
motivation: The paper aims to provide a modular, parallel solver for problems on unbounded domains without artificial boundary conditions, building on an earlier in-house prototype.
method: It maps the radial semi-infinite domain onto a finite interval using associated Legendre functions, employs Fourier series in periodic directions, and distributes computations via MPI with strong and weak scaling up to 512 cores.
result: The solver achieves spectral convergence in diffusion tests, matches the linearized Fisher-KPP front speed within logarithmic corrections, and simulates vortex-pair dynamics with a measured Crow growth rate above theoretical prediction and vortex reconnection.
conclusion: MLegS offers a scalable, modular spectral framework for unbounded-domain PDEs, demonstrated across diffusion, reaction-diffusion, and vortex dynamics examples.

title: A Consistent And Conservative Phase-Field Method For Compressible Multiphase Flows With The Six-equation Model
authors: Ziyang Huang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.18085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the present study, the consistent and conservative Phase-Field method is extended to the six-equation model for compressible multiphase flows. Based solely on the conservation laws and the second law of thermodynamics, the six-equation model with the Phase-Field mechanism is first derived. In addition to satisfying Galilean invariance and consistency of reduction, the model is general to admit an arbitrary number of phases with different formulations of the Phase-Field mechanism. The isobaric closure by the pressure relaxation and the incompressible limit of the proposed model are analyzed. The derivation and analysis identify additional terms arising from the Phase-Field mechanism, which are absent from previous studies. The consistent and conservative numerical approach is adapted to the proposed six-equation model with moderate modifications, retaining the interfacial equilibrium condition, conservation, and flexibility and robustness of incorporating different formulations of the Phase-Field mechanism with bound preservation. As the new component of solving the six-equation model, both the pressure and pressure-temperature relaxations are theoretically analyzed in a general multiphase setup, with a proof of the existence and uniqueness of a thermodynamically admissible solution for these two relaxations. Various two-phase compressible flow benchmarks are performed to demonstrate the method, and good agreement with exact solutions is achieved.
tldr: The paper extends a consistent and conservative phase-field method to a six-equation model for compressible multiphase flows, deriving the model from conservation laws and the second law of thermodynamics and validating it on benchmark two-phase flows.
motivation: Simulating compressible multiphase flows accurately requires models that respect Galilean invariance, reduction consistency, and thermodynamic admissibility, which existing six-equation formulations with phase-field mechanisms do not fully guarantee.
method: The authors derive a six-equation phase-field model from conservation laws and the second law of thermodynamics, analyze isobaric closure, pressure and pressure-temperature relaxations with existence and uniqueness proofs, and adapt a consistent, conservative numerical scheme with bound preservation.
result: The derivation identifies additional phase-field-induced terms absent in prior work, and numerical benchmarks for two-phase compressible flows show good agreement with exact solutions.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a general, thermodynamically consistent and conservative approach for compressible multiphase flows with arbitrary numbers of phases, though it lies outside quantum information science.

title: Van Der Waals Interactions In Supercritical Water Under Earth's Mantle Conditions
authors: Jiajia Huang, Rui Hou, Ding Pan
